deep.reconstruction:
This page sits inside a self-contained section of 1953 notes on Schatten classes of compact operators. Notation: s_p(A)=Σ|λ_i(A)|^p, the sum over eigenvalues; S_p(A)=Σ μ_i(A)^p=‖A‖_p^p, the sum over singular values.

(1) Finishing the proof of inequality (5), Weyl's inequality s_p(A) ≤ S_p(A) for all 0<p<∞.
- On the previous page, Grothendieck treats 0<p<1. The classical bound on zeros of the entire function f(z)=det(1−zA) gives s_p ≤ p²∫_0^∞ log M_A(ρ) ρ^{-p-1} dρ.
- He then uses M_A(ρ) ≤ M_{|A|}(ρ), i.e. |det(1−zA)| ≤ Π(1+|z|μ_i).
- Formula (9) is the exact integral ∫_0^∞ log(1+ρt) ρ^{-p-1} dρ = π t^p/(p sin pπ). It yields (10): s_p(A) ≤ (pπ/sin pπ) S_p(A).
- For general p, choose n with p/n<1 and pass to A^n. The identity s_p(A)=s_{p/n}(A^n) and the n-fold Hölder bound S_{p/n}(A^n) ≤ S_p(A) give s_p(A) ≤ (π(p/n)/sin(π p/n)) S_p(A).
- On this page he lets n→∞. The constant tends to 1, which gives (5).
- This is an 'amplification / power trick': a lossy constant is removed by applying the bound to powers.

(2) Monotonicity: if 0 ≤ H ≤ K (compact, self-adjoint), then S_p(H) ≤ S_p(K). The proof: the decreasing eigenvalue sequence of H is dominated termwise by that of K, by the classical extremal (min–max) characterisation of eigenvalues.

(3) Crossed-out first attempt at the Hölder formula (6): ‖AB‖_r ≤ ‖A‖_p‖B‖_q when 1/p+1/q ≥ 1/r.
- Set L=(AB)(AB)*. Then S_r(AB)=S_{r/2}(L)=S_{r/2m}(L^m).
- Rescale r'=r/2m, p'=p/2m, q'=q/2m, so that again 1/p'+1/q' ≥ 1/r', and try to apply the entire-function formula (9) with k(α)=πα/sin πα.
- The attempt is abandoned and the whole block struck out diagonally. The next page restarts with a direct proof: first ‖A_1⋯A_{2^n}‖_1 ≤ Π‖A_i‖_{2^n} by dyadic induction, which he notes extends to normal traces on von Neumann algebras.
errors: The bound M_A(ρ) ≤ M_{|A|}(ρ), i.e. |det(1+zA)| ≤ det(1+|z||A|), is used on the previous page with its justification left blank '(......)'. Its standard proofs go through exterior powers / Weyl's multiplicative majorization, which already essentially contain inequality (5). The argument is therefore only non-circular if this bound is proved independently; the gap is not filled in the visible text.
Section 3 on this page is abandoned (crossed out), as the author himself recognised. It is replaced by a different proof on the next page.

ideas.what: Proof of Weyl's inequality Σ|λ_i|^p ≤ Σμ_i^p via a zero-counting bound for the Fredholm determinant det(1−zA), the exact integral with constant pπ/sin pπ, and removal of the constant by passing to A^n with n→∞.
ideas.modern_name: Weyl's eigenvalue–singular value inequality; power/amplification ('tensor power') trick
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Weyl 1949 (inequality). The amplification trick is folklore; it was popularised as the 'tensor power trick' by T. Tao.
ideas.where_published: Related material appears in Grothendieck, 'Produits tensoriels topologiques…' (Memoirs AMS 1955) and 'La théorie de Fredholm' (Bull. SMF 1956). Whether this exact proof is printed there is unsure.

ideas.what: Monotonicity of S_p on positive operators via the min–max characterisation of eigenvalues.
Crossed-out attempt to prove Schatten–Hölder by rewriting S_r(AB)=S_{r/2m}(((AB)(AB)*)^m) and rescaling exponents.

missed.claim: The page records a complex-analytic proof of Weyl's inequality: zeros of det(1−zA) are bounded via log M(ρ), and the constant pπ/sin pπ is eliminated by a power trick (A^n, n→∞). This is a different route from Weyl's exterior-power majorization. It is a pleasant early instance of the amplification trick, but not a new result, and similar arguments exist in the eigenvalue-distribution literature.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it shows Grothendieck using a 'tensor power' style trick in 1953. It does not add mathematics absent from the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard results (Weyl's inequality, monotonicity, Schatten–Hölder). The only distinctive feature is the analytic-function proof with the power trick to kill the constant, which is elegant but in the spirit of known Fredholm-determinant methods.
transcription_corrections: First line: the factor is (π p/n)/(sin π p/n), not π(r/p)/sin(π r/p). The left-hand side is probably lowercase s_p(A) (eigenvalue sum).
'Faisant tendre p vers l'infini' should be 'Faisant tendre n vers l'infini'.
The bracket '[-et hermitiennes[?]-]' is a struck-out word, probably 'et hermitiens'; 'positif' is struck out at the start of the next line.
